hypotheses.claim: Durable mechanism credit requires a join of tested head, completed execution steps, successful semantic verdict, receipt bytes, and a repository commit that persists those exact bytes; compute success alone is provisional.
hypotheses.test: Interrupt or delay the persistence lane after successful computation and require the ledger to remain provisional; then complete persistence and verify exactly one state transition without double-counting the compute evidence.
hypotheses.falsifier: A compute-only result provides equivalent durable auditability and replay after artifacts expire, without any persisted receipt or content binding.

hypotheses.claim: Binding sqlite_trust_anchor_sha256 prevents same-library receipts authorized by byte-distinct anchor instances from collapsing into one cohort, but does not prevent coherent rollback of the entire cohort.
hypotheses.test: Hold library/runtime fields constant while varying only anchor bytes; require rejection. Then replay a fully coherent stale cohort to show that independent freshness and semantic restart evidence remain necessary.
hypotheses.falsifier: Different anchor bytes remain safely indistinguishable under the declared deployment trust contract, or the added field alone rejects coherent whole-cohort rollback.

counterhypotheses.counterevidence: The replication job was already successful while its persistence job still had zero executed steps; durable bytes appeared only later in target commit 4e463f9495d304de4e833f6e9e8609baddaf79b2.

counterhypotheses.attack: A synthetically consistent anchor hash can pass a candidate cohort gate without proving root ownership, accepted host, exact service process, real database file descriptors, or restart continuity.
